intent: Re-review the repaired source-only Swift public power detail reader against /tmp/battery-power-full-functionality-gap-audit.md SHA-256 76274bc15a50f2e86673ea8bafc7145753f391117a8f9c60de7daf977816090b. Confirm the prior source-only content/bundle finding and polling-only notification-degradation finding are fully repaired with synthetic proof. Also find any remaining Slice B, public surface, privacy, strict CF, generation, disabled-action, no-live-execution, audit, or false-claim issue. Keep Awake is intentionally excluded.

findings.issue: System and session transition state is updated before checking for an active popup generation, and begin/close do not reset those fields. A sleep, wake, or session event received while the popup is closed can be carried into the next generation with sample/invalidation reset to 1/0, which violates the one-generation/no-last-known-detail story and can surface stale user/session activity in a later popup. The existing synthetic tests cover stale document cache rejection, but not this cross-generation transition leakage.
findings.suggestion: Make transition state generation-scoped: either guard for an active generation before mutating `systemTransition`/`sessionTransition`, or reset both fields to `.unknown` in `beginPopup()` and `closePopup()`. Add a synthetic test where an event is received with no active generation, then a new popup begins and reports `.unknown` transitions.

reviewers.summary: The two prior findings appear repaired: the source-only gate now checks compiled file magic and bundle/build shapes, and the observation driver installs independent invalidations before degrading source notifications to `polling_only` with synthetic heartbeat proof. I still found one material generation/privacy gap: transition state can leak across closed popups, so the repaired tree should not ship until that lifecycle edge is fixed and tested.
